Template 759948 seems to be a C-N bond formation (amide? Actually it's O-B(-O)-aryl and amine). Might not be relevant.

Maybe we can simplify: Use only two steps: Step1 amide formation from anisidine and triazine acid (carboxylic acid). Step2 attach azetidine to benzylic position via SN2 using benzylic bromide and azetidine. The triazine acid already contains the side chain? Actually the triazine acid we got from amide break includes the side chain (Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3). So we need to break that side chain further.

But we could consider that the side chain could be assembled from commercially available 4-bromomethyl phenyl and azetidine. So we need to break C-N bond between benzylic carbon and N of azetidine, giving benzylic bromide and azetidine.

Thus we need a template that breaks C-N bond to give halide and amine. Search for functional_groups_broken=["alkyl halide"]? Actually we want to break C-N to give alkyl halide and amine. Could search for functional_groups_formed=["alkyl halide"] and broken=["secondary amines"].
